title: refactor(terraform/private): split GPU node pools, IAM and networking modules; state layout migration
author: Priya Nair
description: Summary: This PR refactors the terraform/private module set by splitting the monolithic private deployment module into three focused modules: gpu-node-pools, iam-roles, and vpc-networking, and introduces a clearer remote state layout to support per-environment state directories and safer upgrades. Motivation: The previous module combined GPU node pool provisioning, IAM role policies, and networking into a single large module which made iterative changes risky and state transitions brittle. Splitting modules allows isolated changes, faster apply times, and targeted rollbacks for Private deployments. What changed: - New modules/ directory: terraform/modules/private/gpu-node-pool, terraform/modules/private/iam-roles, terraform/modules/private/vpc-networking. Each module has inputs/outputs documented and focused responsibilities. - State layout: moved from a single private/<env>.tfstate to a componentized layout (private/<env>/<component>.tfstate). Migration helper scripts in infra/terraform/scripts/state-migrate.sh are included to move existing state with terraform state mv/import where needed. - IAM: consolidated least-privilege IAM bindings for Private control plane and nodes, introduced module variable to toggle managed KMS roles. - GPU node pools: added node pool taints/labels, node auto-provisioning options, and machine type mapping for commonly used GPU SKUs. - Networking: abstracted subnets, peering and route templates; added optional nat gateway toggle and per-subnet private DNS config. - Tests and CI: added unit tests for modules with terratest harness and a guarded e2e plan run against a non-production test project. Migration notes / upgrade plan: 1) Read the migration guide (terraform/modules/private/README.md and infra/terraform/scripts/state-migrate.sh). 2) Run the migration script in dry-run mode to generate state mv commands. 3) Step the apply: import/move networking state first, then IAM, then GPU pools. 4) We provide roll-forward and rollback instructions in the README; the process requires a short maintenance window for older clusters. Backwards compatibility: We provide compatibility wrappers in terraform/private/legacy.tf which map old module inputs to new modules; however the state layout change requires running the migration script. Rollout plan: staged rollout across environments: staging -> preprod -> prod. Each environment applies are gated behind Infra on-call and CI e2e checks. Testing: - Local terratest runs and CI terraform validate/plan were executed. - E2E provisioning executed in a sandbox project and validated by cluster smoke tests and node GPU detection. Risks and mitigations: - State migration is the primary risk: mitigated by migration script, dry-run, and manual approval steps. - IAM drift: added IAM read-only plan check to CI and manual audit during rollout. Related linear issues: ENG-7891, INF-402.

release_notes:
- Splits private terraform into focused modules: gpu-node-pool, iam-roles, vpc-networking.
- Adds a state migration helper script (infra/terraform/scripts/state-migrate.sh).
- Introduces new per-component state layout: private/<env>/<component>.tfstate.
Upgrade instructions: follow infra/terraform/scripts/state-migrate.sh in dry-run mode, then apply networking -> iam -> gpu pools. Coordinate with Infra on-call for production upgrades.
notes: This PR was coordinated with infra and on-call to minimize disruption. Post-merge follow-ups include telemetry for apply duration and a runbook entry for the state migration process.
